seoTitle: How to Use TradingView Bar Replay for Free in 2026
metaDescription: Turn on TradingView's Bar Replay, fix it when the toolbar won't appear, and see exactly how much intraday history a free plan actually gives you.
intro: Bar Replay lets you rewind a TradingView chart to any earlier point and step forward bar by bar, watching a setup unfold the way it happened instead of judging it in hindsight. This guide covers turning it on from a live chart, what its controls do, and where the real limits sit — which is not quite where most people assume. By the end you'll know which button does what and what to check first when the replay toolbar refuses to appear.

steps.heading: Start from a normal chart before turning on replay
steps.body: Open the instrument you want to practice on — in this walkthrough it's the Dow Jones Industrial Average on a 5-minute timeframe, with the watchlist docked on the right showing other indices and symbols for reference. This is your baseline: a live, unmodified chart with the standard toolbar across the top and drawing tools down the left side. Bar Replay sits among the chart's top-toolbar icons, easy to miss next to the more commonly used indicator and alert buttons.

image.caption: A live TradingView chart before Bar Replay is activated, with the standard toolbar and watchlist visible.

steps.heading: Turn on Bar Replay and pick your starting bar
steps.body: Click the Bar Replay icon and the chart drops into starting-point selection: hover over the price history and a vertical guide follows the cursor. Click the point you want to start from and everything after it disappears from view until you play it back. A new control bar appears at the bottom of the chart with playback controls (step back, play, step forward) and a speed selector currently set to 1x, plus Buy and Sell buttons that let you place simulated trades right from the replay bar, as if you were trading live.

image.caption: Bar Replay's control bar at the bottom of the chart, with Select bar, playback controls, speed, and simulated Buy/Sell buttons.

steps.heading: Set the replay interval for how fast bars reveal
steps.body: Switching to a daily chart and clicking the interval control opens a menu with choices like 1 hour, 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, 1 day, or Auto select interval. This is the amount of time added to the chart with each step of playback — TradingView's own docs describe it as one data update per tick of replay. The options on offer depend on your chart's own timeframe (a 1-minute chart won't offer a 4-hour interval), so it isn't a fully separate setting, but within what's available it lets you blow through a slow multi-month range quickly while still watching each candle form individually instead of jumping straight to the end.

image.caption: The replay interval menu that controls how much time each step advances, scoped to what your chart's timeframe allows.

steps.heading: Step through and place simulated trades
steps.body: With a starting bar and interval chosen, use the play button to run replay forward automatically or the step buttons to advance one bar at a time. The Buy, Sell, and Flatten controls let you open and close a simulated position as price moves, complete with a quantity field and a running order line on the chart — TradingView calls this Replay Trading, and the trade markers it draws on the chart are called Executions. Nothing from a replay session is saved once it ends; it exists only for that run.

image.caption: Bar Replay running on a daily chart, with the Buy, Sell, and Flatten buttons active for simulating a trade in real time.

costNote: Bar Replay doesn't require a paid plan on its own, but how much intraday history you can replay does. A free Basic account gets Bar Replay only on daily-and-higher timeframes; replaying an intraday chart (1-minute, 5-minute, and so on) needs an Essential plan or above. See the table below for what each tier gives you.

troubleshooting.problem: Clicking Bar Replay does nothing — no toolbar appears at the bottom of the chart
troubleshooting.cause: The chart is on a type or symbol Bar Replay doesn't support: Renko, Kagi, Point & Figure, Range, Line Break, Volume Footprint or Time Price Opportunity charts, a spread (formula) symbol, or a symbol converted to a non-default currency.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch to a standard candlestick or bar chart on a regular symbol, then click Bar Replay again.

troubleshooting.problem: The starting bar won't go back as far as I need on an intraday chart
troubleshooting.cause: This is a plan limit rather than a bug. A free Basic account only gets Bar Replay on daily-and-higher timeframes; deeper intraday history needs Essential or a higher plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Switch the chart to a daily timeframe, or upgrade if intraday replay depth is what you actually need.

troubleshooting.problem: Buy/Sell trade markers clutter the chart every time you replay
troubleshooting.cause: Executions and Execution Labels are on by default in Replay Trading.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Settings, go to the Trading tab, and turn off Executions and Execution Labels.

faq.question: Is Bar Replay free on TradingView?
faq.answer: Yes, Bar Replay itself doesn't need a paid plan. What's gated is intraday depth: a free Basic account only replays daily-and-higher timeframes, so 1-minute or 5-minute replay needs an Essential plan or above.

faq.question: Why doesn't the Bar Replay toolbar appear when I click it?
faq.answer: Almost always an unsupported chart type or symbol: Renko, Kagi, Point & Figure, Range, Line Break, Volume Footprint, Time Price Opportunity, a spread symbol, or a currency-converted symbol. Switch to a standard chart type and a regular symbol and try again.

faq.question: What does the replay interval control?
faq.answer: How much time is added to the chart with each step — for example 1 minute or 1 day. The options depend on your chart's own timeframe, and TradingView auto-selects a sensible one when it's set to Auto.

faq.question: Can I place simulated trades during replay without a paid plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Replay Trading's Buy, Sell, and Flatten controls work on a Basic account within whatever timeframe replay is available to you on that plan.

faq.question: What can I do if my plan's replay range isn't long enough?
faq.answer: Scroll the chart manually to the period you want and track price action bar by bar without the automated controls, or build a Pine Script backtesting strategy instead of relying on manual replay. Neither fully replaces Bar Replay, but both work within a free plan while you decide whether upgrading is worth it.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. Plan limits, unsupported chart types, the replay-interval behaviour, and the Executions terminology were re-checked against TradingView's official Help Center in September 2026. That check corrected the article's earlier claim that free-plan replay is limited mainly by how far back you can start — the real free-plan limit is that intraday timeframes aren't replayable at all on Basic, only daily and higher — and added the unsupported-chart-type and Executions-toggle details it didn't previously carry.
